subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
subtype: Approach: switching to an indoor activity [Revision]
passage: Saturday night. Rain! It came at ten, just as we were leaving for the ground. Samir's cousin and I stood at the window for five minutes looking sad. Then Samir said, "What if today is a carrom day?" So it was. Three of us on the floor around the board, and after lunch Nani's ludo box came out, and the fight over the yellow tokens was louder than any cricket match. I lost three games and won one. Pakoras at four while the rain drummed on the tin roof. Cricket next week. Honestly, this felt like a different kind of good day, not a wasted one. Aditi

qa.q: What games did the children play after the rain started?
qa.a: They played carrom on the floor and later ludo.

qa.q: How did Aditi feel by the end of the day?
qa.a: Content, since Aditi calls it a different kind of good day and not a wasted one. 😊

qa.q: What other approach could turn a rained-off day into something good, and why?
qa.a: They could cook something together, like pakoras, or plan the match for next week, because a shared activity keeps spirits up.

qa.q: How might Samir's idea of a carrom day have felt to the others at the window?
qa.a: Probably like a relief, since they were looking sad and Samir gave them something to do straight away.

grounding: Aditi and the others, after rain cancels cricket, switch to indoor games and count it as a different fun day.
